findings.title: /charge-types still names line_item_line_item_type unguarded and the absent-column behaviour is unspecified
findings.where: design.md — "Changed: getChargeTypeBreakdown"; the optional-columns table row for line_item_line_item_type; the error-handling table (no row for this case)
findings.problem: CurAdvancedMetricsService.java:1424 and :1430 select and GROUP BY line_item_line_item_type directly. The design declares a report without that column supported (chargeTypeAvailable=false), guards it in getUnusedCommitment and via basisExpr, but leaves F1's own query unguarded — so /charge-types 502s on a trimmed Data Export. This violates the design's own invariant ("A query never names a column the table lacks") and leaves rule 8's 409/422/200-[] trichotomy unresolved for this case. Reachable from the UI: `available` is undefined while the probe is in flight or has failed (probeState 'unknown', which the design argues is routine), and undefined "renders normally". Whether the fetch is suppressed when available === false is also never stated.
findings.fix: Guard the column and throw ReportCannotAnswerException("the charge type breakdown", List.of("line_item_line_item_type")) -> 422; add the error-table row; state in ChargeTypeReconciliation's behaviour list that available === false renders the unavailable copy INSTEAD of the trigger so no query can ever be issued; add test 15a asserting the throw and that no query is issued.

findings.title: ReportCapabilities' "the column list could not be read" sentences are unimplementable; CurColumnCatalog has no such signal and is not in Files touched
findings.where: design.md — paragraph after the ReportCapabilities record; error-handling table row for /capabilities; edge-case row for information_schema unreadable; CostBasisToggle's 'unavailable' row
findings.problem: CurColumnCatalog exposes only has(...) and present(...), both answered from columns(...), which caches Set.of() for 10 minutes on a failed probe. "Catalog unreadable" and "column genuinely absent" are byte-identical to every caller, so getReportCapabilities cannot write different sentences for them. CurColumnCatalog.java appears in neither the New nor the Modified file list, and test 8 does not cover the unreadable case, so nothing would catch it.
findings.fix: Add `boolean readable(CurSource, CloudAccount) { return !columns(source, account).isEmpty(); }` to CurColumnCatalog (an empty set is only ever a failed probe), add CurColumnCatalog.java to the Modified list, branch the three detail sentences on it, and add test 8a: catalog unreadable -> all flags false and all three details say the list could not be read. If the distinction is not worth the method, delete it from all three places.

findings.title: Build order assigns tests to steps before the endpoints and parameters they exercise exist
findings.where: design.md — "Build order", steps 0 and 1
findings.problem: Step 1 claims tests 28, 29, 30 (/service-resources, built in step 5) and 32, 33 (the basis query parameter and basisOf, built in step 4). Step 0 claims test 35, which asserts 400 on six endpoints including service-resources (step 5) and capabilities (step 1). A coder following the steps writes tests that cannot compile or cannot pass.
findings.fix: Re-assign: step 0 -> 31, 35 (charges-by-service, charge-types, price-vs-volume, resource-change only), 37a-37c. Step 1 -> 1-9, 30 (/capabilities only), 31, 34, 35 (+capabilities), 36, 37, 37d. Step 4 -> add 32, 33. Step 5 -> add 28, 29, 30 (+/service-resources), 35 (+service-resources). State the rule in the preamble: a test lands in the step that introduces the surface it calls.

findings.title: ChargeTypeReconciliation's fetcher snippet does not compile under strict mode, and undefined vs null is unspecified
findings.where: design.md — "New file: ChargeTypeReconciliation.tsx", props block and ledgerKey snippet
findings.problem: fetcher is typed `((...) => ...) | null` and optional, then invoked as `fetcher(a, p, basis)`. frontend-app/tsconfig.json has strict: true and npm run build runs tsc, so this is TS2722/TS18048 and fails `npx tsc --noEmit` (build step 6). Separately, the behaviour list specifies fetcher === null renders nothing but says nothing about the prop being omitted, which is what a direct consumer passes — unlike every sibling component on this card, which defaults its fetcher.
findings.fix: Default it: `fetcher = fetchChargeTypes`, then `const read = fetcher ?? null;`, pass `read && expanded ? accountId : null` to useCurInsight, call through `read`, and `if (!read) return null;` so null and undefined behave alike. Amend test 49 to cover both fetcher={null} and the prop omitted.

findings.title: ChargeTypeReconciliation's insightName value is never specified, so F1's cache key loses the provider discriminator the design requires elsewhere
findings.where: design.md — ChargeTypeReconciliation props (insightName?: string) and the ChargesByServiceSection bullet that renders it
findings.problem: The design states the convention twice (for the capability probe and in the invariants discussion) — keys are derived from insightName "so two providers never share one cache entry for the same account id" — then leaves it unset for the one three-provider feature in the change, where GCP, Azure and AWS all render the component. A coder defaulting insightName = 'charge-types' puts all three in one namespace.
findings.fix: At the call site pass insightName={`${insightName}:charge-types`} (insightName is already `${insightPrefix}charges-by-service`), default it to 'charge-types' in the component with a comment that the parent always overrides, and add to test 66 that the GCP shape's ledger key carries the gcp- prefix.

findings.title: How the card derives `capabilities` from useCurInsight is unspecified; the obvious reading sticks on 'checking' forever after a thrown probe
findings.where: design.md — CostBasisToggle's probeState block; the ChargesByServiceSection capability-probe bullet
findings.problem: probeState keys only off `capabilities`: undefined -> 'checking', null -> 'unknown'. useCurInsight is useQuery with retry: false, which reports data === undefined AND isError === true when the query function throws (network failure). fetchReportCapabilities returns null only on a non-2xx, so the null path covers 409/422/502 but not a throw. If the card passes `data` straight through, a dropped connection renders "Checking what this report can be asked…" for the life of the tab — the exact failure the four-state table exists to rule out. The file's own convention (`isError ? null : (data ?? null)`) handles it, but the design never says to apply it.
findings.fix: Specify the derivation beside the probe-state table: undefined only while capsPending, null when capsError, otherwise caps ?? null. Add a third row to table-driven test 53a: the hook erroring resolves to 'unknown', not 'checking'.

findings.title: BasisNote and ExcludedNote will both render on the amortized basis in the common case — the "two notices for one toggle" shape decision 2 rejected on the tree
findings.where: design.md — decision 2; "ResourceCostDrawer.tsx — changes"; test 71
findings.problem: ExcludedNote fires whenever |excludedCost| >= 0.01, and excludedCost = sumDaily(daily) - currentCost with lineAggregates restricted to line_item_line_item_type = 'Usage'. The code's own comment says that gap is "most of the cost" on a Savings-Plan-covered instance — which is exactly the resource a reader opens on the amortized basis. So the common amortized path stacks two notes in the identical bordered treatment, each explaining a different reason the panel's figures differ from the row that opened it. Decision 2 rejected this shape on the invoice tree ("Two separate notices for one toggle reads as two problems") and did not apply the reasoning here. Placement is also unspecified: ExcludedNote renders twice in the file (ResourceCostDrawer.tsx:437 and :482, once per tab); the design says only "above its figures".
findings.fix: Render BasisNote IN PLACE OF ExcludedNote when basis === 'amortized' && rowCost !== undefined, with its sentence extended to name the excluded charges when |excludedCost| >= 0.01; state that it sits exactly where ExcludedNote does, in both tabs; amend test 71 to assert the two are mutually exclusive rather than independent.

findings.title: The optional-columns table is incomplete about pricing_unit and line_item_line_item_type, so /capabilities would call a report usable while three other sections 502
findings.where: design.md — "Optional columns and the flag each maps to"; "Deliberately not guarded"; "Explicitly out of scope"
findings.problem: pricing_unit is also named unguarded at CurAdvancedMetricsService.java:1155, :1166 (transferCharges) and :1252-:1253 (transferFlows) — /data-transfer, rendered directly beneath this card. line_item_line_item_type is also named unguarded at :249 (usageAndCostByService -> /price-vs-volume, the other tab of this card), :429 (lineAggregates -> /resource-change, the nested drawer) and CurCostDataSource.java:311. So the card reports unitAvailable / chargeTypeAvailable to the client while four other queries on the same two surfaces still fail at Athena analysis time — the same inconsistency used to justify pulling getEffectiveSavingsRate into scope, and the design's own warning about a table that stops being read.
findings.fix: Either guard them (transferCharges/transferFlows take the MAX(pricing_unit)/'' substitution lineAggregates already uses at :408; the two 'Usage' predicates degrade or refuse), or name all five sites in "Explicitly out of scope" and state the consequence: capabilities.unitAvailable and capabilities.chargeTypeAvailable describe this card only, and /data-transfer, /price-vs-volume and /resource-change keep 502-ing on those reports.

findings.title: The vitest harness is unspecified while the Java one is specified in detail, and three tests depend on query-cache identity
findings.where: design.md — "Test matrix — vitest", tests 41-82
findings.problem: The Java preamble specifies the delegating CurInsightCache mock, the lenient() reason and the entitlement stubbing "so no test invents its own". The vitest half gets no harness, yet ~45 cases render components whose hooks are useQuery and therefore need a QueryClientProvider; src/components/Cost/__tests__/ does not exist and the repo has exactly one precedent (src/hooks/useScripts.test.tsx) and no shared helper. Tests 49a, 61 and 65 all measure cache hits under useCurInsight's staleTime of 30 minutes, so a client shared across cases makes them pass or fail for reasons unrelated to the code.
findings.fix: Specify a renderWithQuery helper in the vitest preamble — a fresh QueryClient per test with { retry: false, gcTime: 0 } — add it to the New frontend-app file list, and note that ServiceResourcesDrawer tests also need useLabels / useResourceLabelMap satisfied and that it renders through createPortal.

findings.title: The $2,254-vs-$934 figures cited for endOf are not in the code
findings.where: design.md — controller section, test 36, manual-verification section
findings.problem: CurInsightsController.endOf's comment records $1,107 against $2,367 with a $1,260 difference. The $76.42-vs-$86.01 citation is real (scopePredicate's javadoc); this one is not.
findings.fix: Use $1,107 vs $2,367 in all three places so the coder looking for the comment finds it.

findings.title: basisOf(String) has no signature and no error-rendering sibling
findings.where: design.md — controller change 1
findings.problem: parsePeriod is specified as Optional<YearMonth> with a companion invalidPeriod(period). basisOf is named only as "a basisOf(String) helper the handlers call", with the 400 body given but no return type — and a helper returning CostBasis cannot also return the 400.
findings.fix: Mirror the period pair: private Optional<CostBasis> basisOf(String raw) plus private ResponseEntity<Map<String,String>> invalidBasis(String raw), so both parameters are validated the same way in the same place.

findings.title: Validation ordering in the handlers is unspecified
findings.where: design.md — controller section; input validation summary; error-handling table
findings.problem: denyIfNotEntitled, parsePeriod, basisOf and the service non-blank / <=128 checks all return different statuses, and no precedence is stated except for resourceChange's resourceId.isBlank(). It decides whether an unentitled caller sending basis=amortised gets 400 or 404.
findings.fix: State the order once — denyIfNotEntitled, then parsePeriod, then basisOf, then endpoint parameters — and note that entitlement first is what keeps the endpoint from being an existence oracle.

findings.title: denyIfNotEntitled's javadoc contradicts its own chosen call site
findings.where: design.md — the denyIfNotEntitled snippet and "The three call sites…" paragraph
findings.problem: The javadoc says "Call this from an HTTP handler, BEFORE insightCache.getOrCompute", and the chosen sites are withSource(...), resourceChange(...), priceVsVolume(...), capabilities(...). withSource is a private plumbing helper, not a handler — which is where the guard belongs, but the wording tells the next reader to move it.
findings.fix: Reword: "Call this on the request thread, before insightCache.getOrCompute — from a handler, or from withSource, which is the shared prologue for ten of them."

findings.title: Tests 68 and 75 are not assigned to any build step

findings.title: ChargesByServiceSection's default for scopedResourcesFetcher is not stated

findings.title: The demoTopResources groupCount rationale no longer holds for AWS

findings.title: fetchReportCapabilities' shape check does not validate the flags

findings.title: Duplicate rows for service='Other' are not in the edge-case table
findings.where: design.md — Edge cases, "A report that genuinely carries Other as a product name"
findings.problem: getServiceResources keeps product_product_name in the GROUP BY (correctly, for row-shape parity) and servicePredicate('Other') matches NULL, '' and the literal 'Other'.
